theme: 3 terms on Auto Layout basics: the rule-based layout system, one rule about a view's size or position, and the short way to write that rule for one edge

terms.definition: The UIKit system that sizes and places views from rules you give it, instead of fixed frames.
terms.example: Use Auto Layout here, the card has to fit every iPhone size.

terms.definition: One rule about a view's size or position, like keeping its left edge 16 points from its parent.
terms.example: Add a Constraint for the height, the banner view is collapsing to zero.
terms.code:
let c = NSLayoutConstraint(
    item: label, attribute: .leading,
    relatedBy: .equal, toItem: view,
    attribute: .leading,
    multiplier: 1, constant: 16)
c.isActive = true

terms.definition: A property such as `leadingAnchor` that builds a rule for one edge or size of a view in a short, type-safe way.
terms.example: Use a Layout Anchor instead of the old initializer, it's much easier to read.

video.title: Auto Layout, Constraint & Layout Anchor | Day 84
video.description:
Learn to explain how UIKit places views with rules: Auto Layout, Constraint & Layout Anchor, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Auto Layout - The UIKit system that sizes and places views from rules you give it, instead of fixed frames.
Constraint - One rule about a view's size or position, like keeping its left edge 16 points from its parent.
Layout Anchor - A property such as `leadingAnchor` that builds a rule for one edge or size of a view in a short, type-safe way.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.description:
Explain Auto Layout, Constraint & Layout Anchor in UIKit by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
오토 레이아웃, 제약 조건, 레이아웃 앵커 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Auto Layout - The UIKit system that sizes and places views from rules you give it, instead of fixed frames.
한국어: 오토 레이아웃: 고정된 frame 대신 개발자가 준 규칙으로 뷰의 크기와 위치를 정하는 UIKit 시스템

Constraint - One rule about a view's size or position, like keeping its left edge 16 points from its parent.
한국어: 제약 조건: 예를 들어 왼쪽 가장자리를 부모에서 16포인트 떨어뜨리는 것처럼, 뷰의 크기나 위치에 관한 규칙 하나

Layout Anchor - A property such as `leadingAnchor` that builds a rule for one edge or size of a view in a short, type-safe way.
한국어: 레이아웃 앵커: `leadingAnchor`처럼 뷰의 가장자리나 크기 하나에 대한 규칙을 짧고 타입 안전하게 만드는 프로퍼티

In this video, Mina and Jake find out why a label never shows up and the console complains about constraints, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

landscape.hook: Your label never shows up. Can you explain why in English?

dialogue.title: Where did my label go?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, my `label` never shows, and the console says unable to satisfy constraints.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Did you set up Auto Layout for it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes, I activate one Constraint, built with a Layout Anchor.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The Constraint looks fine. But UIKit adds its own ones too.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You never turned off `translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints`, so the old frame becomes extra rules.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And they fight with my top Constraint?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. The frame says zero, your Constraint says 20.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So I set that flag to false, and Auto Layout uses only mine?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Then add a leading anchor too, one Layout Anchor per edge.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Flag off first, then each Layout Anchor works with Auto Layout.
Fixed frames ignore screen size, Auto Layout adapts.
